report.title: Conference-talk and video-transcript source class: is the extraction cost worth the yield?
report.question_or_target: Measured over a fixed 20-item sample, how many distinct, non-duplicate mechanisms does a video/talk transcript produce per 10k tokens of extraction cost, compared with the blog-post and official-docs classes over the same subject matter - and does it clear the threshold to stay in the default source-class set?
report.answer: On the frozen 20-subject .NET Conf 2022 matched sample, official-docs yield 0.663517 distinct non-duplicate mechanisms per 10k extraction-request tokens, transcripts 0.417823, and blogs 0.259372. Transcripts out-yield blogs and under-yield official docs. Cost is prompt_tokens+completion_tokens of one o200k_base-tokenized extraction request per item (instruction + topic codebook + document, plus JSON response), not a source-only payload tokenization. The three companion-source paraphrases that previously inflated transcript-only counts (handler lifecycle, WPF/WinForms Blazor Hybrid modernization, Blazor loading progress) are shared. T02 and T14 restatement talks collapse against their companion blogs. No numeric default-set retention threshold exists in the catalog, REGISTER.md, or CLAIM-REGISTRY.json, so threshold clearance is NOT-CHECKED and no default-set membership change is authorized.
